title: Alistair Cockburn and the Naming of Hexagonal Architecture (2005)
explainer: Years before Robert C. Martin popularized "Clean Architecture," Alistair Cockburn had been sketching, since the mid-1990s, a design where the database and the UI both sit outside the application core as peers, rather than the database anchoring the bottom of a layered stack. He wrote the idea up on his blog in 2005 and picked the hexagon mainly to escape the top/bottom bias of layered diagrams; by his own account the shape and the number six were never meant to be significant, and he later favored the more literal name "ports and adapters." That lineage is why Clean Architecture's dependency rule (business logic depends on nothing outer) reads as an older idea under a newer name.
